decision_conditions: Condition : 1 - The proposal amounts to inappropriate development within the site which is identified as Local Open Space and that special circumstances do not exist to justify overriding presumption against such development. Therefore the proposal is considered to be contrary to policy ENV-N1.11 (Protection and Improvement of Local Open Space) of the Council's Revised Deposit Unitary Development Plan.

Condition : 2 - The proposed development would, by reason of its siting, scale and access arrangement, represent backland development of the site and would have an adverse effect on the amenities of the adjoining residential properties and would be incompatible with the character of the area, contrary to policies ENV1.1 (All New Development), H.1.2 (Housing Standards and Guidelines) and H.3.3 (Backland/Infill Developments) of the Council's Unitary Development Plan and policies ENV-B.1.1 (New Development), H.4.1 (Housing Standards and Guidelines) and H.6.3 (Backland Development/Infill Development) of the Revised Deposit Unitary Development Plan.

Condition : 3 - The proposed development is likely to result in the loss of TPO trees on the site, would not conserve and enhance established habitats in the area and is detrimental to the visual amenity and character of the locality and the Hanworth Park Conservation Area. The proposal would be contrary to policies ENV.1.9 (Trees and Community Woodlands), ENV.1.10 (Tree Preservation Orders), ENV.1.2 (Conservation Areas) and ENV.5.4 (Habitat Protection) of the UDP and policies ENV-N.2.7(Trees and Community Woodlands), ENV-N.2.8 (Tree Preservation Orders) and ENV-N.2.4 (Habitat Protection) of the Revised Deposit UDP.

Condition : 4 - The proposed development is within the Hanworth Park Conservation Area and it fails to preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the conservation area and is considered to be contrary to policy ENV.1.2 (Conservation Areas) of the Unitary Development Plan and policy ENV-B.2.2 (Conservation Areas) of the Revised Deposit Unitary Development Plan.

Condition : 5 - The proposed access road is considered to be too narrow and likely to compromise traffic and pedestrian safety and be prejudicial to the free flow of traffic. The proposal would be to be contrary to policy T.3.6 (Road Safety) of the UDP and policy T.4.4 (Road Safety) of the Revised Deposit UDP.
description: Demolition of existing dwelling (no.10) and development of 6 x four bedroom houses and 1 x five bedroom house, new access, pedestrian link, open space area and landscaping
